title: Balloon Pop
tagline: Pop smiley, heart, bunny and star balloons over a sunny countryside!
howToPlay: A friend asks for balloons: pop the ones they want (4 blue ones, the hearts, 3 then 2 more, 3 red and 2 blue, or the balloons with 5 dots) and tap 🧺 Give when the basket is just right. Too many? Tap a balloon in the basket to let it go. Then choose a treat for the picnic. When all eight friends are at the picnic, everyone waves. Stuck? The friend helps with numbered slots. Confident counters move on to plain slots, then ten-frames, the teens, one more / one less and making two bunches the same. 🌱 Start easy goes back to the beginning.
learning: Counting to 10, colours, shapes, adding on and matching dots to quantities

title: Bumper Ducks
tagline: Bonk, bounce and squeak! Up to 4 rubber ducks in bumper boats grab bubbles and stars.
howToPlay: Drag anywhere (or use the arrow keys) to paddle your duck. Tap 💨 (or Space) to dash and BONK! In Pond helpers every duck fills one shared ten-frame together: fill the tens or find the bubbles of one colour, then count them up. 🎁 boxes make you giant, super fast or bouncy. Pick ⏱️💥 Race for the lively 90-second round. Nobody is ever out!
learning: Counting in tens (place value), sorting by colour, cooperation and spatial awareness

title: Bunny Hop
tagline: Hop Pip the bunny home through meadows, mushrooms, autumn woods and snow!
howToPlay: Tap the screen or press the space bar to hop, and tap again in the air for a flippy double hop. Pip needs carrots for winter: some hang at hop height (hop as each one comes) and some grow in the grass (stay down to munch them). Once Pip is catching whole rows, his basket asks for fewer carrots than the row holds: count them in, then let the rest go by. Too many, and the basket is too heavy: one rolls out. Logs, rocks, pumpkins and carrots come in patterns with their own notes; when a ? appears, pick what comes next, then keep the pattern going through the mist: hop for the obstacles and stay down for the carrots. A wrong pick plays the pattern again for another go, and right answers lead on to three-part and growing patterns. At home, Pip's pantry shows each place's crates; answer his question about them (a line of carrots helps you count on), then see if there are enough for winter. After each pattern, wild flowers grow in the grass: stay down to pick them, and at home plant them by Pip's door in a pattern of your own, which Pip sings back. Choose 🐢 for a slower trip.
learning: Counting, comparing and adding, reading and making patterns, and timing

title: Cake Stack
tagline: Stack yummy cake layers into a giant birthday cake for your animal friends!
howToPlay: Each birthday friend orders a cake in pictures, from the bottom layer to the top: listen to the order, then wait for the matching layer and tap, click or press Space to drop it when it lines up. Layers the order doesn't need yet just slide past. Later friends order patterns like strawberry, mint, strawberry, mint. Blow out the candles, then share the cake fairly: give every friend the same number of slices. Choose 🎂 Free stacking to drop any layer, or open Recipe studio to build pictured recipes and share equal slices.
learning: Sequencing, patterns, counting and equal sharing

title: Crash Racers
tagline: Race up to 4 cars through Ubud, Helsinki and Montreal. Crashes welcome!
howToPlay: 📦 Deliver: drive slowly round a picture town with four parcels. Tap a parcel to load it, find its matching house on the big map (🍎 fruit shop, 🌸 florist, 🐶 dog's house…), then drive there to hand it over. ↩️ turns you round for a shorter way. At the end, see the route you chose. 🏁 Race and 💥 Smash! are still there for lively play with friends: steer with the arrows or on-screen buttons, and 🔊 turns the sound off.
learning: Map reading, matching and route planning

title: Dragon Glide
tagline: Fly Ember the baby dragon through floating sky islands, cloud rings and rainbow waterfalls!
howToPlay: Drag anywhere (or use the arrow keys) to steer Ember the dragon home through four sky worlds. Each world has one goal, shown as a picture and spoken: fly through numbered rings in order (1 to 5, then 1 to 10), or gather the right hearts, stars or moons into your basket. Missed a ring? It waits for you. At each nest Ember's family sorts and counts what you brought home, and waits until you tap to fly on. Tap 🔥 to light lanterns and pop bubbles.
learning: Number order, counting to 10, sorting by colour and shape, and steering

title: Fish Pond
tagline: Go fishing with Bear and fill your book with fish, a puffer, a whale and treasure!
howToPlay: Pick a place: sunny lake, sunset river, starry night, icy sea or coral reef. Bear asks a riddle ("something with a hard shell"): tap the animal that fits, and it comes to your line. When the bobber dips and a ! pops up, tap to reel it in. An animal that fits goes in your 📖 book; one that doesn't is put back gently, with the reason why. Can you find all 18? Older players get trickier riddles, two clues at once, and Bear's list: animals to find in other waters, so you choose where to fish.
learning: Observation, animal habitats (fresh water and sea) and counting

title: Memory Match
tagline: Flip the cards and find the matching animal twins!
howToPlay: Tap two cards to turn them over and hear each animal's name. Find all the matching pairs! Choose how they match: 🐶🐶 twins (on the big boards some twins wear a 🎀 bow or a 🧢 hat, so look closely), 🐮🔊 an animal and its sound (the speaker card says "Moo!": who says that?), 🐮 and its baby (a cow's baby is a calf; on the bigger boards the babies sleep in baskets and you only hear and see their name, so find whose baby it is), or 🐮🐷🐥 Homes for older children: keep turning over the animals that live together on the farm, at home, wild on land or in the water. Tap 👀 once a round to peek. Boards grow from 2 pairs to 10, and the next board follows how carefully you remembered. 📖 My animals keeps what you found out about each animal: its sound, its baby and its home.
learning: Visual and auditory memory, looking closely, animal names and the sounds they make, baby animal words (and which parent each belongs to), and sorting animals by where they live (including that some fit more than one home)

title: Paint Splash
tagline: Roll giant paint rollers with up to 4 friends and paint a picture together!
howToPlay: Drag anywhere (or use the arrow keys) to roll your animal's paint roller. A dashed chalk shape asks for a colour ("Paint the fish green!"), but the pots only hold 🔴🟡🔵, so work out the mix and paint it like a painter, in coats: one paint all over inside the lines, then the other on top while it is still wet and shiny. Swapping pots back and forth still mixes, but careful coats are what move the puzzles on. Red and yellow make orange, yellow and blue make green, red and blue make purple, all three make brown. Painted shapes are inked and kept safe while robot friends paint a frame round the page. The recipe is pictured at first; as you paint carefully it hides behind ❓, two-part shapes (a tree's leaves and trunk) arrive, then puzzles with more than one answer ("a mix of blue and one more paint"), and finally puzzles on two-part shapes and with two conditions ("a mix with blue but no red"). After each shape you pick the next one from the card, and every few shapes you choose the colour yourself. Stuck? A ring shows the pot to try. When the page is full, keep painting on a fresh page. There is no clock: tap 🖼️ Finished! when your picture is done, and it is kept in My pictures by itself. Choose ⏱️ Quick for 75 seconds of free painting with 🌈 rainbow and 💧 water puddles, or open Mix my colours for the colour studio.
learning: Colour mixing with primaries (secondary colours and brown), reasoning from a rule to a colour (including two conditions and elimination), planning in coats while the paint is wet, staying inside the lines, and cooperation

title: Penguin Bowling
tagline: Belly-slide a chubby penguin down the ice and knock over snowmen and fish!
howToPlay: Swipe up (or pull back and let go) to slide the penguin down the ice. A curvy swipe makes it curve! On a keyboard, ← → aim and Space slides; ◀ ▶ move the penguin. Bumpers 🛟 keep the penguin out of the gutters. After every roll, tap each pin still standing to count it (fallen ones don't count): fallen and standing always make 10. Children who count carefully are asked for the missing part instead (7 + ? = 10, or ? + 2 = 10), first from three numbers, later from a 1–10 strip, and may plan each fresh rack: pick 'knock 8, leave 2' and choose where to stand (the middle knocks nearly all, the edge just one; footprints help at first). The strongest counters work the bond out while a snow cloud hides the pins, and may try bumpers down. Before a second roll, say where the pins are or which side has more: footprints show where to walk the penguin, fewer of them as the child grows, until the spare is their own plan. Tap 💭 to guess how many will fall first. Pick 5 frames for a shorter game.
learning: Number bonds to 10, counting, predictions and spatial reasoning

title: Rocket Garage
tagline: Snap together a silly rocket, then blast your animal pilot off to the Moon and beyond!
howToPlay: Tap or drag parts from the tray to build your rocket: nose cones, windows, fuel tanks, fins, boosters and stickers (tap the rocket to swap a part, tap a colour to paint it). Press the big red button to launch! When you change a part, guess first: will it go farther, the same, or less far? (Later, name the very planet.) Watch last time's rocket fly beside yours, then hear what your change did. A wobbly rocket rocks on the pad and sways in flight; a steady one stands still. Every discovery goes into your 📓 notebook, which remembers where each booster landed and which noses, tanks and fins you found wobbly 〰️ or steady ━ (the tray marks them too), and its 🧪 workshop races rocket A against rocket B. Steer to the stars out at the sides: fifteen make the ⚡ turbo ready, and you choose whether to zoom one planet farther. After a few flights Robot hands you mission cards. First guess where the rocket on the pad lands as it is, then change parts to reach his planet. Missions grow from landing on a planet, to landing there steady or wobbly, to fixing Robot's own rocket with just one change, to his rocket with two faults (or two wobbly parts), fixed one change per flight. Then the workshop holds a race challenge: one steady and one wobbly rocket to the same planet.
learning: Design comparisons, predictions, experimentation and planning with two variables

title: Star Catcher
tagline: Fly Kitty’s rocket past friendly planets and catch the falling stars!
howToPlay: Drag your finger or mouse, or use the arrow keys, to fly Kitty's rocket. Stars fall in little rows, each carrying a number: steer to the one that comes next to light the next star of a real constellation. The rule stays under the sky panel with the numbers in order. A wrong pick floats away and the right star shows itself, so careful choices build the sky sooner. At each planet your child joins the dots in counting order (tap, or arrow keys and Enter); above the first level a number or two hides as "?" and your child picks the missing one. Then they choose the next shape, and each card carries its own way of counting, so they choose to stay steady or take a stretch. Each sequence starts somewhere new, and as your child gets steady the numbers move from matching to counting on and back, twos, fives, big numbers where 13 sits beside 31, jumps of ten, finding the pattern, and big jumps like 9 or 11. At home, find each constellation again by its shape or by how it was counted.
learning: Number order, counting on and back, skip counting, missing numbers in a sequence, place value with tens, number patterns and two-digit jumps, reading two-digit numbers, real constellations and star patterns
